commands.run: scripts/test --tool sqruff --suite dialects --suite rules --suite autofix --suite templater --jobs 4
commands.extract: uv run --frozen --project harness python scripts/s3/s1_by_base.py extract --checkout CLONE CLONE/out/report.json
commands.build: uv run --frozen --project harness python scripts/s3/s1_by_base.py build

row: total: cases; pass, fail, error, skip: cases with that status; checks.<check>: of the cases where the check applies, pass, fail, and no_result; needs_python (templater): cases with the tag, and how many pass. Groups: dialects by dialect, rules by the rule codes of the case, autofix by dialect, templater by fixture folder.

sqruff.note: Per-case data: results/s3/sqruff-cases.json, a new local run of the 4 suites (commands.run) at harness.commit. Its counts agree with the S1 summary and its failed cases are those of known_failures/sqruff.txt. Failure reasons: the reason prefixes of known_failures/sqruff.txt (sqll-harness known-failures --counts). 'no_result': the check applies to the case but has no result (an unsupported item, an earlier failure, or an unknown result). The build checks the suite totals and the failed cases against other committed files. The failure reasons are the text of known_failures/sqruff.txt; extract checks that the run gives this text. No other committed file has the check values of each failed case, thus the check values of each group come from this run only. The proof of them is that a new run gives the same per-case file.

sqlfluffrs.note: sqlfluff-rs is sqlfluff 4.4.0 with use_rust_parser and use_rust_rules (harness/sqlfluff-rs.md). Its parser is generated from the sqlfluff grammar and gives 2306 of 2306 exact dialect trees. But Python sqlfluff drives it: the CLI, the config, the templaters, and the rules are Python; only CP01, CP03, and CP04 have a Rust detection. Thus these results prove the generated parser, not a standalone tool. The S1 data have no per-case list for sqlfluff-rs: each case passes (known_failures/sqlfluff-rs.txt is empty, passed = total in the summary), so the case lists and the checks of each case come from the pinned fixtures; their counts agree with the summary.

new-parser.note: Option 3 has no implementation, thus it has no S1 data. The decision record gives estimates for it, labelled as estimates (T9).
